summary: Over-generate 12 candidates, pick top-7 in Swift
hypothesis: Generating more candidate questions (12) than needed and selecting the best 7 via a deterministic Swift scorer should yield higher-quality output than a single-shot generate, because a larger candidate pool gives the ranker more to work with and filters weaker questions before output.
technique: A single on-device FM call over-produces 12 candidate questions, then a deterministic Swift coverage/ranking scorer selects the top 7 for output — no additional model calls involved.
result: Scored 0.263 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), with rubric atom=5, spec=3, cover=2, nat=3, nonRed=4. Coverage collapsed to 2 despite high atomicity, indicating the expand+select approach does not reliably surface dimension-spanning questions; discarded.
label: exp002
